Summarise the Immunity of a Model State

Source: R/immunity_history.R
summarise_immunity.Rd

Summarises who is susceptible and who is immune, and why, in a model state.

Usage

summarise_immunity(state, params, R0)

Arguments

state

A list of arrays `S`, `E`, `I`, `R`, `Is` and `Rc` (age by stratum by risk group), as returned by `dust2::dust_unpack_state()`.

params

The parameter list the state was produced with (for the contact matrix and vaccine protection).

R0

Basic reproduction number to use for the effective reproduction number.

Value

A list with `reff` (see [effective_reproduction_number()]), `population`, `susceptible` (effective susceptibility as a share of the population), `vaccinated` (share in any vaccinated stratum), `infected` (number currently infected) and `by_age`, a data frame with the shares above for each age group.

Details

Everyone falls into one of four groups, which sum to one within each age group:

`susceptible_unvaccinated`

Never infected and unvaccinated (or protection fully waned).

`susceptible_vaccinated`

Never infected, vaccinated but not protected: the share `1 - m` of those in a vaccinated stratum with protection `m`.

`immune_vaccine`

Never infected and protected by vaccination: the share `m` of those in a vaccinated stratum.

`immune_infection`

Infected now or in the past (whether or not vaccinated).

`susceptible` is the sum of the first two (effective susceptibility).
